summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill creates a new intelligence agency to replace an existing one.
The new agency would lead and coordinate the national intelligence community and report directly to the Prime Minister.
The bill also expands the agency's assessment and evaluation roles beyond those of the office it replaces.
changes: Establishes the Office of National Intelligence as a statutory agency within the Prime Minister's portfolio.
Transfers the functions, roles, and staff of the Office of National Assessments to the new agency.
Gives the new agency leadership over the national intelligence community, including coordination and evaluation duties.
Allows the agency's head to issue directions and guidelines to intelligence agencies.
Continues the National Assessments Board and sets rules for secrecy and privacy.
summary.affected: The national intelligence community, including traditional intelligence agencies and the intelligence functions of several government departments and law enforcement bodies.

speeches.speaker: Christian Porter
speeches.brief: The Office of National Intelligence Bill 2018 establishes the Office of National Intelligence (ONI) to replace the Office of National Assessments, headed by a secretary-level director-general who will advise the Prime Minister and lead the expanded National Intelligence Community (NIC) with enterprise management, coordination and evaluation authority but not operational control over agencies. The bill implements recommendations from the 2017 Independent Intelligence Review, appoints Nick Warner as director-general designate, and expands the NIC to include the Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission, Australian Federal Police, Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre, Department of Home Affairs, and Department of Defence.

speeches.speaker: Christian Porter
speeches.brief: The Office of National Intelligence (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2018 amends 19 acts, repeals the Office of National Assessments Act 1977, and establishes the Office of National Intelligence (ONI) with access to information, oversight by the Parliamentary Joint Committee on Intelligence and Security and the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security, access to the assumed identities regime, and cooperation with ASIO, ASIS, AGO, and ASD. The bill includes transitional provisions for the change from ONA to ONI.

speeches.speaker: Mark Dreyfus
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Office of National Intelligence Bill 2018 and related legislation, which implement recommendations from the 2017 Independent Intelligence Review to establish the Office of National Intelligence to lead Australia's intelligence agencies and replace the Office of National Assessments, and urged the government to also act on two further review recommendations regarding the Parliamentary Joint Committee on Intelligence and Security.

speeches.speaker: Tim Wilson
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Office of National Intelligence Bill 2018 and related legislation are critical for strengthening parliamentary oversight, supporting amendments that expand scrutiny by the Parliamentary Joint Committee on Intelligence and Security and the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security, and called for greater accountability of agencies like the Australian Taxation Office.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: The Office of National Intelligence Bill 2018 and its consequential bill were argued to be needed to implement the 2017 Independent intelligence review recommendations, establishing the Office of National Intelligence (ONI) to coordinate intelligence, advise the Prime Minister, and integrate capabilities across the national intelligence community. Four government amendments from the Parliamentary Joint Committee on Intelligence and Security will enhance transparency, particularly in the privacy rules.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: The speaker presented a supplementary explanatory memorandum and moved government amendments (1) to (4) to the Office of National Intelligence Bill 2018 and the Office of National Intelligence (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2018.
